sanskrit: evam uktā tadā kanyā tena rājñā tadāśrame uvāca hasatī vākyam idaṃ sumadhurākṣaram
english: Thus addressed by the king there in the hermitage, the maiden spoke these words with a smile, in syllables most sweet.

sanskrit: kaṇvaṣyāhaṃ bhagavato duḥṣanta duhitā matā tapasvino dhṛtimato dharmajñasya yaśasvinaḥ
english: "O Duṣyanta, I am considered the daughter of the blessed Kanva — the ascetic, the steadfast, the knower of dharma, the illustrious one."

sanskrit: duḥṣanta uvāca ūrdhvaretā mahābhāgo bhagavāṃl lokapūjitaḥ caled dhi vṛttād dharmo 'pi na calet saṃśitavrataḥ
english: Duṣyanta said: "The blessed one is of supreme greatness, a practitioner of ūrdhvaretas, worshipped by the world — for even dharma might deviate from its course, but one of sharpened vow does not deviate."

sanskrit: kathaṃ tvaṃ tasya duhitā saṃbhūtā varavarṇinī saṃśayo me mahān atra taṃ me chettum ihārhasi
english: "How have you, O fair-complexioned one, come to be his daughter? I have a great doubt in this matter; please resolve it for me here."

sanskrit: śakuntalovāca yathāyam āgamo mahyaṃ yathā cedam abhūt purā śṛṇu rājan yathātattvaṃ yathāsmi duhitā muneḥ
english: Shakuntala said: "How this account came to me, and how it came to pass in former times — hear it truly, O king, how I am the daughter of the sage."

sanskrit: ṛṣiḥ kaś cid ihāgamya mama janmābhyacodayat tasmai provāca bhagavān yathā tac chṛṇu pārthiva
english: "A certain seer came here and prompted the account of my birth; the blessed one related it to him — hear it as it is, O lord of the earth."

sanskrit: tapyamānaḥ kila purā viśvāmitro mahat tapaḥ subhṛśaṃ tāpayām āsa śakraṃ suragaṇeśvaram
english: "In former times, so it is said, Viśvāmitra was performing great austerities, and greatly afflicted Śakra, the lord of the hosts of gods."

sanskrit: tapasā dīptavīryo 'yaṃ sthānān māṃ cyāvayed iti bhītaḥ puraṃdaras tasmān menakām idam abravīt
english: "Fearing that this one, whose power blazed with asceticism, might dislodge him from his position, Purandara said this to Menaka:"

sanskrit: guṇair divyair apsarasāṃ menake tvaṃ viśiṣyase śreyo me kuru kalyāṇi yat tvāṃ vakṣyāmi tac chṛṇu
english: "'O Menaka, you excel among the apsarases in divine qualities — do me a benefit, O auspicious one; hear what I shall tell you.'"

sanskrit: asāv ādityasaṃkāśo viśvāmitro mahātapāḥ tapyamānas tapo ghoraṃ mama kampayate manaḥ
english: "'That Viśvāmitra, radiant as the sun, of great austerity, performing terrible penance — he makes my mind tremble.'"

sanskrit: menake tava bhāro 'yaṃ viśvāmitraḥ sumadhyame saṃśitātmā sudurdharṣa ugre tapasi vartate
english: "'O slender-waisted Menaka, this Viśvāmitra is your task — he of sharpened soul, most difficult to assail, engaged in fierce austerity.'"

sanskrit: sa māṃ na cyāvayet sthānāt taṃ vai gatvā pralobhaya cara tasya tapovighnaṃ kuru me priyam uttamam
english: "'So that he may not dislodge me from my position, go to him and entice him — create an obstacle to his austerity; do this best favor for me.'"

sanskrit: rūpayauvanamādhuryaceṣṭitasmitabhāṣitaiḥ lobhayitvā varārohe tapasaḥ saṃnivartaya
english: "'With beauty, youth, sweetness, gestures, smiles and speech — captivate him, O shapely one, and turn him away from his austerities.'"

sanskrit: menakovāca mahātejāḥ sa bhagavān sadaiva ca mahātapāḥ kopanaś ca tathā hy enaṃ jānāti bhagavān api
english: Menaka said: "That blessed one is always of great splendor, great in austerity, and wrathful — for even the blessed lord himself knows this about him."

sanskrit: tejasas tapasaś caiva kopasya ca mahātmanaḥ tvam apy udvijase yasya nodvijeyam ahaṃ katham
english: "You yourself tremble before his splendor, his austerity, and his wrath — that great-souled one — then how could I not tremble?"

sanskrit: mahābhāgaṃ vasiṣṭhaṃ yaḥ putrair iṣṭair vyayojayat kṣatre jātaś ca yaḥ pūrvam abhavad brāhmaṇo balāt
english: "He who deprived the greatly blessed Vasiṣṭha of his beloved sons, and who, though born a kshatriya, became a brahmin by force of will —"

sanskrit: śaucārthaṃ yo nadīṃ cakre durgamāṃ bahubhir jalaiḥ yāṃ tāṃ puṇyatamāṃ loke kauśikīti vidur janāḥ
english: "— who, for purposes of purification, created a mighty river with many waters, which people know in the world as the most sacred Kauśikī —"

sanskrit: babhāra yatrāsya purā kāle durge mahātmanaḥ dārān mataṅgo dharmātmā rājarṣir vyādhatāṃ gataḥ
english: "— where, in a time of difficulty long ago, the righteous royal sage Mataṅga, gone to the condition of a hunter, supported this great-souled one's wife —"

sanskrit: atītakāle durbhikṣe yatraitya punar āśramam muniḥ pāreti nadyā vai nāma cakre tadā prabhuḥ
english: "— where, in a time of famine in the past, the sage returned to his hermitage and the lord then gave the name 'Para' to the river —"

sanskrit: mataṅgaṃ yājayāṃ cakre yatra prītamanāḥ svayam tvaṃ ca somaṃ bhayād yasya gataḥ pātuṃ śureśvara
english: "— where he himself, with joyful mind, performed the sacrifice for Mataṅga, and out of fear of whom, O lord of heroes, you went to drink soma —"

sanskrit: ati nakṣatravaṃśāṃś ca kruddho nakṣatrasaṃpadā prati śravaṇapūrvāṇi nakṣatrāṇi sasarja yaḥ
english: "— who, in anger, created new lunar asterisms with richness of stars, surpassing the existing stellar lineages, the constellations beginning with Śravaṇa —"

sanskrit: etāni yasya karmāṇi tasyāhaṃ bhṛśam udvije yathā māṃ na dahet kruddhas tathājñāpaya māṃ vibho
english: "These are the deeds of him before whom I greatly tremble — command me, O lord, so that when angered he does not burn me."

sanskrit: tejasā nirdahel lokān kampayed dharaṇīṃ padā saṃkṣipec ca mahāmeruṃ tūrṇam āvartayet tathā
english: "He could burn the worlds with his splendor, shake the earth with his foot, compress mighty Meru, and quickly set it spinning."

sanskrit: tādṛśaṃ tapasā yuktaṃ pradīptam iva pāvakam katham asmadvidhā bālā jitendriyam abhispṛśet
english: "How could a young woman like me touch one such as he — endowed with austerity, blazing like fire, his senses fully mastered?"

sanskrit: hutāśanamukhaṃ dīptaṃ sūryacandrākṣitārakam kālajihvaṃ suraśreṣṭha katham asmadvidhā spṛśet
english: "He whose face is the sacrificial fire, who blazes, whose eyes are the sun and moon and whose tongue is time itself, O best of gods — how could one like me touch him?"

sanskrit: yamaś ca somaś ca maharṣayaś ca; sādhyā viśve vālakhilyāś ca sarve ete 'pi yasyodvijante prabhāvāt; kasmāt tasmān mādṛśī nodvijeta
english: "Yama and Soma and the great seers, the Sādhyas, the Vishvadevas, and all the Vālakhilyas — even these tremble before his power; why then should one like me not tremble?"

sanskrit: tvayaivam uktā ca kathaṃ samīpam; ṛṣer na gaccheyam ahaṃ surendra rakṣāṃ tu me cintaya devarāja; yathā tvadarthaṃ rakṣitāhaṃ careyam
english: "Being thus commanded by you, O king of gods, how could I not go near the seer? But think of protection for me, O lord of the gods, so that I may act protected for your sake."

sanskrit: kāmaṃ tu me mārutas tatra vāsaḥ; prakrīḍitāyā vivṛṇotu deva bhavec ca me manmathas tatra kārye; sahāyabhūtas tava devaprasādāt
english: "Let the wind strip away my garment there while I am at play, O god; and let Manmatha be my helper there in that task, by your divine grace."

sanskrit: vanāc ca vāyuḥ surabhiḥ pravāyet; tasmin kāle tam ṛṣiṃ lobhayantyāḥ tathety uktvā vihite caiva tasmiṃs; tato yayau sāśramaṃ kauśikasya
english: "And let a sweet-scented wind blow from the forest at that time, as I tempt the sage." Having said 'so be it' and having arranged all this, she then went to the hermitage of Kauśika.

sanskrit: śakuntalovāca evam uktas tayā śakraḥ saṃdideśa sadāgatim prātiṣṭhata tadā kāle menakā vāyunā saha
english: Shakuntala said: "Thus addressed by her, Śakra instructed the wind of eternal passage, and Menaka then departed at the appointed time along with the wind."

sanskrit: athāpaśyad varārohā tapasā dagdhakilbiṣam viśvāmitraṃ tapasyantaṃ menakā bhīrur āśrame
english: "Then that shapely, timid Menaka saw Viśvāmitra performing austerities in the hermitage, his sins burnt away by asceticism."

sanskrit: abhivādya tataḥ sā taṃ prākrīḍad ṛṣisaṃnidhau apovāha ca vāso 'syā mārutaḥ śaśisaṃnibham
english: "Having saluted him, she then played before the sage, and the wind carried away her garment, white as the moon."

sanskrit: sāgacchat tvaritā bhūmiṃ vāsas tad abhiliṅgatī utsmayantīva savrīḍaṃ mārutaṃ varavarṇinī
english: "She, the fair-complexioned one, rushed swiftly to the ground to grab that garment, seemingly smiling with shyness at the wind."

sanskrit: gṛddhāṃ vāsasi saṃbhrāntāṃ menakāṃ munisattamaḥ anirdeśyavayorūpām apaśyad vivṛtāṃ tadā
english: "That best of sages then saw Menaka, flustered, clutching her garment, her age and beauty beyond description, her form revealed."

sanskrit: tasyā rūpaguṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā sa tu viprarṣabhas tadā cakāra bhāvaṃ saṃsarge tayā kāmavaśaṃ gataḥ
english: "Seeing the excellence of her beauty, that bull among brahmin seers then formed the intent to be with her, falling under the sway of desire."

sanskrit: nyamantrayata cāpy enāṃ sā cāpy aicchad aninditā tau tatra suciraṃ kālaṃ vane vyaharatām ubhau ramamāṇau yathākāmaṃ yathaikadivasaṃ tathā
english: "He invited her, and she, the blameless one, was willing; those two spent a very long time in the forest, delighting together according to their desire as though it were but a single day."

sanskrit: janayām āsa sa munir menakāyāṃ śakuntalām prasthe himavato ramye mālinīm abhito nadīm
english: "That sage fathered Shakuntala upon Menaka on the lovely slopes of the Himālayas, near the river Malini."

sanskrit: jātam utsṛjya taṃ garbhaṃ menakā mālinīm anu kṛtakāryā tatas tūrṇam agacchac chakrasaṃsadam
english: "Having delivered the child and abandoned the newborn along the Malini, Menaka, her task accomplished, then quickly went to Śakra's assembly."

sanskrit: taṃ vane vijane garbhaṃ siṃhavyāghrasamākule dṛṣṭvā śayānaṃ śakunāḥ samantāt paryavārayan
english: "Seeing that newborn lying in the desolate forest teeming with lions and tigers, birds surrounded it on all sides."

sanskrit: nemāṃ hiṃsyur vane bālāṃ kravyādā māṃsagṛddhinaḥ paryarakṣanta tāṃ tatra śakuntā menakātmajām
english: "The flesh-eating, meat-craving predators of the forest did not harm this child — the birds guarded her there, that daughter of Menaka."

sanskrit: upaspraṣṭuṃ gataś cāham apaśyaṃ śayitām imām nirjane vipine 'raṇye śakuntaiḥ parivāritām ānayitvā tataś caināṃ duhitṛtve nyayojayam
english: "I went there to touch the sacred waters, and I saw her lying in the desolate wilderness, surrounded by birds; I then brought her and appointed her as my daughter."

sanskrit: śarīrakṛt prāṇadātā yasya cānnāni bhuñjate krameṇa te trayo 'py uktāḥ pitaro dharmaniścaye
english: "He who made the body, he who gave life, and he whose food one eats — these three in turn are called fathers in the settled teaching of dharma."

sanskrit: nirjane ca vane yasmāc chakuntaiḥ parirakṣitā śakuntaleti nāmāsyāḥ kṛtaṃ cāpi tato mayā
english: "And because she was protected by birds in the desolate forest, I gave her the name 'Shakuntala' then and there."

sanskrit: evaṃ duhitaraṃ viddhi mama saumya śakuntalām śakuntalā ca pitaraṃ manyate mām aninditā
english: "Thus know her as my daughter, O gentle one — Shakuntala — and the blameless Shakuntala considers me her father."

sanskrit: etad ācaṣṭa pṛṣṭaḥ san mama janma maharṣaye sutāṃ kaṇvasya mām evaṃ viddhi tvaṃ manujādhipa
english: "This he related when questioned by the great seer regarding my birth — thus know me as Kanva's daughter, O lord of men."

sanskrit: kaṇvaṃ hi pitaraṃ manye pitaraṃ svam ajānatī iti te kathitaṃ rājan yathāvṛttaṃ śrutaṃ mayā
english: "Not knowing my true father, I consider Kanva my father — thus have I told you, O king, the account as I heard it occurred."

sanskrit: duḥṣanta uvāca suvyaktaṃ rājaputrī tvaṃ yathā kalyāṇi bhāṣase bhāryā me bhava suśroṇi brūhi kiṃ karavāṇi te
english: Duṣyanta said: "It is entirely clear that you are a princess, O auspicious one, speaking as you do — be my wife, O shapely one; tell me, what shall I do for you?"

sanskrit: suvarṇamālā vāsāṃsi kuṇḍale parihāṭake nānāpattanaje śubhre maṇiratne ca śobhane
english: "Gold garlands, garments, earrings, ornaments, beautiful shining cloth from many towns, splendid jewels and gems —"

sanskrit: āharāmi tavādyāhaṃ niṣkādīny ajināni ca sarvaṃ rājyaṃ tavādyāstu bhāryā me bhava śobhane
english: "— all this I shall bring you today, and golden ornaments and animal skins; let the entire kingdom be yours today — be my wife, O lovely one."

sanskrit: gāndharveṇa ca māṃ bhīru vivāhenaihi sundari vivāhānāṃ hi rambhoru gāndharvaḥ śreṣṭha ucyate
english: "Come to me, O timid one, O beautiful one, through the Gandharva form of marriage — for among marriages, the Gandharva is said to be the best, O you with thighs like plantain stems."

sanskrit: śakuntalovāca phalāhāro gato rājan pitā me ita āśramāt taṃ muhūrtaṃ pratīkṣasva sa māṃ tubhyaṃ pradāsyati
english: Shakuntala said: "My father has gone from this hermitage to gather fruits, O king — wait a moment; he will give me to you."

sanskrit: duḥṣanta uvāca icchāmi tvāṃ varārohe bhajamānām anindite tvadarthaṃ māṃ sthitaṃ viddhi tvadgataṃ hi mano mama
english: Duṣyanta said: "I desire you, O shapely one, O blameless one who inclines toward me; know that I am here for your sake — my mind has gone to you."

sanskrit: ātmano bandhur ātmaiva gatir ātmaiva cātmanaḥ ātmanaivātmano dānaṃ kartum arhasi dharmataḥ
english: "The self alone is one's own kinsman, the self alone is one's own path, the self alone is one's own refuge — you should give yourself in accordance with dharma."

sanskrit: aṣṭāv eva samāsena vivāhā dharmataḥ smṛtāḥ brāhmo daivas tathaivārṣaḥ prājāpatyas tathāsuraḥ
english: "Eight forms of marriage in total are remembered as sanctioned by dharma: Brahmā, Daiva, Arsha, Prajapatya, and also Asura —"

sanskrit: gāndharvo rākṣasaś caiva paiśācaś cāṣṭamaḥ smṛtaḥ teṣāṃ dharmān yathāpūrvaṃ manuḥ svāyaṃbhuvo 'bravīt
english: "— Gandharva, Rākṣasa, and Paiśāca as the eighth. Manu Svāyaṃbhuva proclaimed the dharmic rules for these in proper order."

sanskrit: praśastāṃś caturaḥ pūrvān brāhmaṇasyopadhāraya ṣaḍ ānupūrvyā kṣatrasya viddhi dharmyān anindite
english: "Know that the first four are commended for a brahmin; know that for a kshatriya six in order are righteous, O blameless one."

sanskrit: rājñāṃ tu rākṣaso 'py ukto viṭśūdreṣv āsuraḥ smṛtaḥ pañcānāṃ tu trayo dharmyā dvāv adharmyau smṛtāv iha
english: "The Rākṣasa form is also said to be valid for kings; the Asura is remembered for Vaiśyas and Śūdras. Of the five, three are righteous; two are remembered as unrighteous here."

sanskrit: paiśācaś cāsuraś caiva na kartavyau kathaṃ cana anena vidhinā kāryo dharmasyaiṣā gatiḥ smṛtā
english: "The Paiśāca and the Asura should never be performed under any circumstance; by this rule one should act — this is remembered as the path of dharma."

sanskrit: gāndharvarākṣasau kṣatre dharmyau tau mā viśaṅkithāḥ pṛthag vā yadi vā miśrau kartavyau nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: "The Gandharva and Rākṣasa forms are both righteous for a kshatriya — have no fear of them; whether separately or combined, they may be performed — there is no doubt in this."

sanskrit: sā tvaṃ mama sakāmasya sakāmā varavarṇini gāndharveṇa vivāhena bhāryā bhavitum arhasi
english: "You who are desirous and I who am desirous — O fair-complexioned one, you deserve to become my wife through the Gandharva form of marriage."

sanskrit: śakuntalovāca yadi dharmapathas tv eṣa yadi cātmā prabhur mama pradāne pauravaśreṣṭha śṛṇu me samayaṃ prabho
english: Shakuntala said: "If this is indeed the path of dharma, and if I am indeed master of my own giving — then hear my condition, O best of the Pauravas, O lord."

sanskrit: satyaṃ me pratijānīhi yat tvāṃ vakṣyāmy ahaṃ rahaḥ mama jāyeta yaḥ putraḥ sa bhavet tvadanantaram
english: "Promise me truly what I shall tell you in private: the son who is born of me shall be your heir after you."

sanskrit: yuvarājo mahārāja satyam etad bravīhi me yady etad evaṃ duḥṣanta astu me saṃgamas tvayā
english: "He shall be crown prince, O great king — tell me this truthfully; if it be so, O Duṣyanta, let there be union between you and me."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam astv iti tāṃ rājā pratyuvācāvicārayan api ca tvāṃ nayiṣyāmi nagaraṃ svaṃ śucismite yathā tvam arhā suśroṇi satyam etad bravīmi te
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: "'So be it,' the king replied to her without hesitation, 'and I shall also bring you to my own city, O bright-smiling one — as you deserve, O shapely one; I tell you this truly.'"

sanskrit: evam uktvā sa rājarṣis tām aninditagāminīm jagrāha vidhivat pāṇāv uvāsa ca tayā saha
english: "Having said this, that royal sage took the hand of that blameless-gaited one according to the rite, and dwelt together with her."

sanskrit: viśvāsya caināṃ sa prāyād abravīc ca punaḥ punaḥ preṣayiṣye tavārthāya vāhinīṃ caturaṅgiṇīm tayā tvām ānayiṣyāmi nivāsaṃ svaṃ śucismite
english: "Having reassured her, he departed and said again and again: 'I shall send the four-division army for your sake; with it I shall bring you to my own home, O bright-smiling one.'"

sanskrit: iti tasyāḥ pratiśrutya sa nṛpo janamejaya manasā cintayan prāyāt kāśyapaṃ prati pārthivaḥ
english: "Having thus promised her, O Janamejaya, that king, lord of the earth, departed, pondering in his mind as he went toward Kaśyapa."

sanskrit: bhagavāṃs tapasā yuktaḥ śrutvā kiṃ nu kariṣyati evaṃ saṃcintayann eva praviveśa svakaṃ puram
english: "'What will the blessed one endowed with austerity do upon hearing of this?' — thinking thus, he entered his own city."

sanskrit: muhūrtayāte tasmiṃs tu kaṇvo 'py āśramam āgamat śakuntalā ca pitaraṃ hriyā nopajagāma tam
english: "After some time had passed, Kanva too returned to the hermitage; but Shakuntala, out of shame, did not go to meet her father."

sanskrit: vijñāyātha ca tāṃ kaṇvo divyajñāno mahātapāḥ uvāca bhagavān prītaḥ paśyan divyena cakṣuṣā
english: "Then Kanva, of divine knowledge and great austerity, perceived the situation; the blessed one, pleased, spoke having seen all with his divine eye."

sanskrit: tvayādya rājānvayayā mām anādṛtya yatkṛtaḥ puṃsā saha samāyogo na sa dharmopaghātakaḥ
english: "'What you have done today, disregarding me, uniting with a man of royal lineage — that union is not a violation of dharma.'"

sanskrit: kṣatriyasya hi gāndharvo vivāhaḥ śreṣṭha ucyate sakāmāyāḥ sakāmena nirmantro rahasi smṛtaḥ
english: "'For the Gandharva form of marriage is called the best for a kshatriya — performed in private, without mantras, between two who desire each other.'"

sanskrit: dharmātmā ca mahātmā ca duḥṣantaḥ puruṣottamaḥ abhyagacchaḥ patiṃ yaṃ tvaṃ bhajamānaṃ śakuntale
english: "'Duṣyanta, the best of men, is righteous-souled and great-souled — you have gone to that highest of men as husband with devotion, O Shakuntala.'"

sanskrit: mahātmā janitā loke putras tava mahābalaḥ ya imāṃ sāgarāpāṅgāṃ kṛtsnāṃ bhokṣyati medinīm
english: "'A great-souled and mighty son shall be born to you in the world — one who shall enjoy this entire earth bounded by the ocean.'"

sanskrit: paraṃ cābhiprayātasya cakraṃ tasya mahātmanaḥ bhaviṣyaty apratihataṃ satataṃ cakravartinaḥ
english: "'And the wheel of that great-souled universal emperor shall roll forward unchecked, ever victorious.'"

sanskrit: tataḥ prakṣālya pādau sā viśrāntaṃ munim abravīt vinidhāya tato bhāraṃ saṃnidhāya phalāni ca
english: "Then she washed his feet, and having set down the load and placed the fruits nearby, she spoke to the rested sage."

sanskrit: mayā patir vṛto yo 'sau duḥṣantaḥ puruṣottamaḥ tasmai sasacivāya tvaṃ prasādaṃ kartum arhasi
english: "'The one I have chosen as my husband is that Duṣyanta, the best of men — please bestow your grace upon him together with his ministers.'"

sanskrit: kaṇva uvāca prasanna eva tasyāhaṃ tvatkṛte varavarṇini gṛhāṇa ca varaṃ mattas tatkṛte yad abhīpsitam
english: Kanva said: "I am indeed already pleased with him for your sake, O fair-complexioned one; receive from me the boon you desire on his account."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato dharmiṣṭhatāṃ vavre rājyāc cāskhalanaṃ tathā śakuntalā pauravāṇāṃ duḥṣantahitakāmyayā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: "Then Shakuntala, desiring the welfare of Duṣyanta, chose righteous conduct and steadiness in the kingdom for the Pauravas."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca pratijñāya tu duḥṣante pratiyāte śakuntalā garbhaṃ suṣāva vāmoruḥ kumāram amitaujasam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: "After Duṣyanta had made his promise and departed, Shakuntala, she of beautiful thighs, gave birth to a son of immeasurable might."
